responses.tool-purpose: Creates levelled reading materials and follow-up activities from source text.
responses.problem-solved: It reduces the time needed to adapt reading materials for mixed-ability groups.
responses.feature-interest: Turning one article into multiple reading levels with quick comprehension questions.
responses.test-request: We asked Diffit to turn a short article on constructive alignment into versions for different learner levels.
responses.test-what-happened: It produced differentiated reading passages with vocabulary support and several usable question ideas.
responses.surprised: The speed of generating scaffolded questions was better than expected.
responses.corrected: We rewrote a few questions because some prompts were too generic and one summary missed an important nuance.

strengths.text: Quickly differentiates reading materials for mixed ability groups.
Provides a strong starting point for comprehension activities.

weaknesses.text: Some generated questions are too broad without teacher editing.

opportunities.text: Useful for producing adapted pre-class reading tasks.

threats.text: Teachers may over-trust the quality of generated summaries.

responses.learning-improve: It could help students access the same concept at different reading levels without waiting for manual rewriting.
responses.teacher-time: Preparing differentiated reading packs and starter questions.
responses.strongest-use: Rapid preparation of scaffolded reading tasks for seminars.
responses.avoid-use: When exact disciplinary wording matters and oversimplification would distort the concept.
responses.check-before-use: Check the accuracy of summaries, question quality, and whether simplification removed important meaning.

quadrant-map.rationale: High time saving with moderate risk because outputs still need teacher review.

responses.ai-decisions: It chose which ideas to foreground, what vocabulary to simplify, and how to frame comprehension questions.
responses.human-judgement-needed: An educator still needs to judge whether the adapted text preserves conceptual accuracy and matches learner needs.
responses.concerned: An inexperienced educator might accept the simplified version without noticing where meaning has been flattened.
responses.other-educators-know: It is best treated as a drafting partner rather than a finished classroom resource.
responses.view-change: We expected it to be mostly a worksheet generator, but it felt more useful as a differentiation tool.
